feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear progression and relevant public-sector depth. It reads polished and substantive, but it is slightly repetitive and could sharpen impact by reducing overlap, tightening phrasing, and adding more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, culminating in leadership roles that support credibility and show increasing scope.  
- Strong domain alignment: digital platforms, governance, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are consistently reinforced.  
- Good use of scale indicators and concrete details such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; the current structure repeats similar content and weakens clarity.  
- Add more results-oriented outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more evidence of business/user impact would strengthen them (e.g., engagement gains, efficiency improvements, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists is inconsistent (some bullets use serial commas, some do not); “French (A2/Learning)” is awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. Tightening it will improve scanability and sharpen impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Make the first sentence more direct and outcomes-oriented: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years driving web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger verbs like “leading,” “scaling,” or “modernizing.”
- Trim the second sentence into a tighter capability summary: “Leads enterprise web, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Consider aligning wording with the subtitle by using “digital platform” rather than “digital leader” for consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance models,” “content operations,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Public-sector communications” is already reinforced throughout the NACo experience section.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinct will improve scanability and reduce repetition.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and sharpen broad items:
  Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” for clearer meaning and stronger alignment with the AI search project.
- Change “Multi-channel” to “Cross-channel” or “Integrated” for a more senior, strategic tone.
- Keep this section capability-focused; avoid tool-specific language already covered in Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” repeat almost verbatim from the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills’ “Public-sector and advocacy messaging.”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use a cleaner list format with parallel verbs and less jargon: “Designed,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched.”
- Tighten wording: “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is enough; cut “AI-enabled” twice in the same item.
- Add one concrete result, audience, or scale detail per project where available to make these feel less generic.
- Revise for consistency: use “10 x 20-foot” (not “10×20-foot”) and keep punctuation/style uniform across all entries.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with the NACo roles in Work Experience; consider framing these as selected examples rather than restating responsibilities.
- “Built” appears twice; vary verbs to avoid repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your NACo director role and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “advise,” “deliver”) with action + result phrasing: “Redesigned workflows,” “launched modular microsites,” “improved governance,” “led AI search prototype/initiative.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets grouped by impact: platform/campaign builds, operations/governance, AI search. Add metrics if possible: number of sites/toolkits launched, users served, publishing time reduced, search accuracy/engagement gains.
- Emphasize consultant positioning: cross-functional advisory, implementation leadership, and short-term modernization initiatives rather than ongoing channel ownership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia” repeats prior NACo leadership language.
- Microsites and AI search also appear in Recent Projects; keep this item higher-level and save specifics for the project section.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with good scale metrics; it should read more like an executive achievement entry and less like a channel inventory. Emphasize transformation, team leadership, and business outcomes while trimming overlap with earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest wins into sharper bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add budget size, team size, reporting improvements, production savings, engagement growth, or faster publishing/decision-making.
- Tighten channel language: replace “including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands…” with a result such as audience growth, open/click rates, campaign performance, or production volume.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership and modernization.
- Video studio/build-out may partially duplicate footer project examples; keep one concise bullet here and let projects show detail.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps heavily with the more senior NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scope so it shows how this role set up the later director-level impact.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership and scale: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground measurable scope: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-oriented: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with direct action: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial coordination/workflows” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version tactical, not governance-heavy.
- “Weekly advocacy video update” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; clarify this entry as expansion/scaling rather than launch.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should sharpen the highest-value leadership signals and use more distinctive phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad labels with tighter, senior-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy campaigns & stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy & planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” if you want stronger alignment with recent role language.
- If space allows, add one differentiator such as “AI-enabled content discovery strategy” to reflect current consulting work and recent projects.
- Keep all items noun-based and parallel; avoid vague phrases like “audience-focused” unless paired with “strategy” or “planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; vary wording or cut one.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over exhaustive software naming.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters; keep only the most relevant platforms:  
  **Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery**
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially **jQuery**, unless it is central to current target roles.
- Use broader phrasing like **enterprise CMS platforms** if you want to imply WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages without listing all four again.
- If space allows, sharpen impact language: **CMS modernization and scalable content architecture** or **search and discovery experiences**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Technical + IT**; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- **AI-enabled search experiences** already appears in Core Competencies; consider varying to **AI-enabled discovery** or removing here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize higher-value analytical leadership and decision support, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • Web performance and SEO analysis • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Put the most strategic items first: lead with KPI design, executive/leadership reporting, and analytics strategy before listing platforms.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding” or “Executive reporting” for clearer, stronger phrasing.
- If space allows, align with recent impact from NACo: “Analytics infrastructure and executive reporting” to echo the GA4/BigQuery/Power BI work without repeating full bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and Technical + IT more tool-specific.
- “SEO and performance analysis” partially overlaps with broader analytics/reporting language; consider consolidating as “web performance analysis.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and recent NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, more distinctive capabilities tied to recent leadership-level multimedia work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task-level to capability-level language: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows • Virtual event production”
- Consider replacing “video production and editing” with “broadcast-quality video production” to better match the studio build-out in the 2022–2024 role.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Livestream and hybrid event delivery for advocacy programming and member events”
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing broad categories (“studio operations”) with narrow tools unless the tool is a differentiator, as PTZ likely is.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one instance.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps heavily with “event delivery”; combine to avoid repetition.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Since Drupal is central to the most recent roles, this item should better reflect depth and recency.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider emphasizing Drupal as primary.
- Add light proficiency framing: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, split by strength: **Primary: Drupal | Working knowledge: WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep platform names only; avoid repeating broader phrases like “CMS modernization” here since that belongs elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider deleting one section or making this one more platform-specific.
- Drupal/modernization impact is already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so don’t restate those outcomes here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior, recent CV, this item should emphasize implementation tools you actively use and group them more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from coding languages alone to practical delivery: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Separate modern tooling/infrastructure: “Technical implementation: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope or level to avoid sounding junior, e.g. “front-end troubleshooting, tag deployment, lightweight serverless scripting, deployment automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills
- GTM also overlaps conceptually with analytics/infrastructure; keep it here only if this section is meant to be tool-specific

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more category-driven.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize systems ownership, not just apps: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana/Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Consider renaming the heading to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems”
- Group overlapping project-management tools to save space and reduce list fatigue: “Jira/Asana/Trello” instead of listing each separately
- If accurate, add one short qualifier for impact: “used to support cross-team planning, approvals, and automated content workflows”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies, so avoid overloading this item with the same language
- Basecamp may feel dated/less relevant unless it was used recently; consider dropping it in favor of recency and stronger tools like Power Automate/Zapier

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use and enterprise relevance, especially since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to add scope/positioning, e.g.: **Email & Engagement Platforms:** Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, strengthen with qualifiers: **Enterprise email automation and member engagement platforms:** Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest platform experience first; if NACo work relied most on Higher Logic, list that first.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie one platform to outcome-based use (segmentation, newsletter operations, journey automation, member communications), since tool names alone undersell impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with Work Experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating platform names in multiple role bullets unless tied to a measurable result.
- “Engagement” also overlaps conceptually with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-focused.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it to emphasize analysis/optimization capabilities rather than repeating platform names already evidenced in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • Experimentation**
- Replace vague terms like **Dashboarding** with outcome-oriented skill language such as **KPI reporting**, **performance analysis**, or **executive reporting**
- If accurate, consider upgrading **A/B testing** to **Experiment design / A/B testing** to sound more strategic and senior

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider merging or making one tools-only and the other outcomes-focused
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already called out in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid overloading this section with the same phrasing

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, since leadership, governance, and scaled operations are already covered in newer entries.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-build impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates for member and advocacy communications.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “coordinated the work of a digital media associate” or “mentored a junior digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement, or publishing volume.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with the 2018–2024 roles; keep this version lighter on governance language.
- “Weekly video updates” is repeated in the next role; frame this as launching or early producing if accurate.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, innovation support, and the podcast as the clearest distinctive outcome.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest result: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific support verb: “produced multimedia and digital content assets for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so the progression is clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/multimedia bullets; keep the focus here on podcast launch and innovation/research coordination.
- Avoid repeating broad digital leadership language already covered in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mixed capability list than a tightly scoped tools section. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already emphasized elsewhere, so this entry should stay software/tool-focused.

Suggested edit
- Rename or tighten to emphasize tools: “Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
- If you want to keep workflows, separate tools from production capabilities: “Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio operations • Podcast recording/editing”
- Use more specific phrasing than “workflows”; “studio operations,” “switching/streaming,” or “recording/editing” is stronger and more concrete.
- If accurate, add one higher-value tool/platform used in studio production instead of generic workflow language.
